run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T09:17:40Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert's error signal is real and localized: frontend-proxy error spans (operation 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress') rose from ~1-4 per 5 minutes before 09:17 to ~661 per 5 minutes at 09:27, and its access logs show HTTP 500 on /api/data via_upstream. The errors originate one hop deeper: frontend's error spans are GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', the client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and tcp.connect; frontend's own CPU throttling (~0.30) and memory (~126-129 MB of 200Mi) were unchanged across the window. The ad service is the only backend whose spans collapsed (GetAds completions ~280/5m at 09:18 to zero from 09:23) while every other otel-demo backend kept serving normally. On the ad container itself I observed the failure mechanics: the JVM's reported CPU utilizations jumped to ~1.0-1.3, container CPU usage climbed to exactly its 50m limit, CFS throttling went to ~100% of periods from 09:22, memory working set climbed to 522-642 MB against a 450Mi limit with a ~100x jump in container_memory_failures_total, and the container was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 09:17:09 and restarted at 09:17:10; ad's own GetAds p95 latency grew 91ms -> 253 -> 301 -> 366 -> 593 -> 1000ms before it stopped completing spans, while frontend's remaining GetAds client spans fail almost all within 2ms, i.e. immediate rejection rather than timeout. In the same seconds a Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos (namespace chaos-mesh) began spawning JVMChaos experiments against exactly otel-demo/ad-554b849958-fcl25 container ad (first 'Successfully apply chaos' 09:16:44, repeated through 09:25:41, each ~45s). That schedule is the object that applied the fault; the exact injected JVM action cannot be read with the available tools. Contributing conditions observed on the ad Deployment: no readiness/liveness/startup probe and very tight limits (50m CPU / 450Mi), so the kubelet kept the pod Ready and in the Service endpoints while the JVM was starved.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error spans rose from a background of ~1-4 per 5 minutes (1.1-4.4 in the 5-minute windows ending 09:15-09:17) to 138.9 (window ending 09:19), 353.3 (09:21), 610 (09:23), 608.9 (09:25) and 661.1 (09:27); the affected frontend-proxy operations are 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR.

frontend-proxy access logs after 09:20:48 show repeated HTTP 500 responses on /api/data (e.g. "GET /api/data?contextKeys=telescopes HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream) toward the frontend upstream; the pre-incident log lines 08:52-09:10 were only sparse 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started entries, i.e. background.

The frontend service's own error spans are zero until 09:17, then 281.1 (5-minute window ending 09:19), 707.8 (09:21), 1225.6 (09:23), 1208.9 (09:25) and 1324.4 (09:27); the erroring frontend operations are GET, GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and tcp.connect.

frontend's client calls to grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds switched from all non-error (296.7 per 5 minutes, 0 errors up to the window ending 09:18) to errors: 67.8 (09:19), 123.3 (09:20), 173.3 (09:21), 302.2 (09:23), 330 (09:27), while its non-error GetAds calls fell to 0 by 09:23.

At 09:28 the frontend's failing GetAds client spans complete almost immediately: of 256.7 spans increased over 5 minutes, 226.5 are in the le=2.0ms bucket and the whole distribution ends at le=400ms, so these are fast rejections, not long client timeouts.

The ad service's own server spans show the failure from the provider side: oteldemo.AdService/GetAds completions fell from 280 per 5 minutes (window ending 09:18) to 160 (09:20), 44.2 (09:22) and 0 from 09:23 onward, with the same collapse in getAdsByCategory and getRandomAds, while its GetAds p95 latency grew from 91.1ms (09:17) to 253ms (09:18), 366ms (09:20), 593ms (09:21), 1000ms (09:22) and then had no completing spans.

The ad container (pod ad-554b849958-fcl25, container ad) was CPU-saturated against its own limit: container CPU usage rose from ~0.005-0.008 cores through 09:16 to ~0.045-0.050 cores from 09:21 onward (limit 50m) and the throttled-periods ratio rose from ~0.08-0.22 (09:00-09:17) to 0.858 (09:20), 0.960 (09:21), 0.999 (09:22) and ~1.0 through 09:28; the JVM's jvm_cpu_recent_utilization_ratio for opentelemetry-demo/ad moved from ~0.23-0.46 to 1.317 (09:16) and 0.986 (09:17+).

The ad container was under severe memory pressure: container_memory_working_set_bytes went from ~310 MB (through 09:16) to 522 MB (09:18), 609 MB (09:19) and 642 MB (09:22) against a 450Mi limit, and the 10-minute increase of container_memory_failures_total (scope=container) jumped from ~3.9k (09:10-09:14 windows) to 120,565 (09:18), 283,239 (09:20), 625,462 (09:24) and 784,757 (09:26).

The ad container's previous instance terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 at finishedAt 2026-11-17T09:17:09Z (startedAt 08:40:08Z), restartCount is 1, the new container started at 09:17:10Z and the pod's Ready condition lastTransitionTime is 09:17:10Z; the pod resource spec is requests cpu 10m/memory 225Mi, limits cpu 50m/memory 450Mi.

A Chaos Mesh Schedule named otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos in namespace chaos-mesh started spawning JVMChaos experiments against otel-demo/ad-554b849958-fcl25 container ad at 09:16:34Z (otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos-4c7dg), with 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-fcl25/ad' at 09:16:44Z and further jobs at 09:17:34, 09:18:45, 09:19:41, 09:20:37, 09:21:34, 09:22:47, 09:23:44, 09:24:42 and 09:25:41, each reported Applied then Recovered after ~45s, with 'Forbid spawning' events when the prior job was still running.

The ad Deployment has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe on the ad container, so pod Ready state does not reflect application health; the ad Service still selects opentelemetry.io/name=ad and its Endpoints list the pod IP 100.96.4.112:8080 even while the service was failing.

The ad service was still handling requests normally right up to the restart: its container logged 'Targeted ad request received ...' continuously from at least 09:11:28 through 09:17:06 (548 matching lines in 09:07-09:18), and no exception, OutOfMemory, byteman, chaos or GC lines were found in its logs for 09:10-09:18.

Only the ad service lost its spans; cart, checkout, product-catalog, payment, shipping, quote, recommendation, currency, email and accounting span counts continued through 09:27 with no new error series, and the otel-collector's throttling ratio stayed ~0.12-0.14, so the missing ad spans are not a collector-wide pipeline failure.

The frontend container's resources did not change with the incident: its CPU throttling ratio stayed ~0.294-0.330 and its memory working set ~126-129 MB (limit 200Mi) from 09:00 to 09:28, while its span volume stayed ~15,000 per 5 minutes.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo currently stores the ad fault-injection flags adFailure, adHighCpu and adManualGc with defaultVariant "off" (state ENABLED), and all otel-demo pods except load-generator run on node i-06e4f0f4f681d7e45, where the other services kept working normally.

A separate earlier restart happened before the error signal deviated: the fraud-detection container was OOMKilled with exitCode 137 at finishedAt 2026-11-17T08:54:41Z (restartCount 1, currently ready, limits 100m/400Mi), and its error spans remained at only ~1.1 per 5 minutes throughout.

Leading explanation: the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos (chaos-mesh) is what broke the ad service. Its first 'Successfully apply chaos' on otel-demo/ad-554b849958-fcl25/ad is at 09:16:44Z, 25s before the ad container's OOMKill (09:17:09Z) and about a minute before frontend-proxy errors appear in the window ending 09:19; the experiments then re-apply every ~60s, matching the sustained ~100% CPU throttling, the JVM CPU ratio near 1.0 and the continuing GetAds failure after the 09:17:10 restart. The exact injected action (CPU/memory stress, GC, latency or exception) cannot be confirmed from the readable data.

Contributing condition: the ad Deployment's tight limits (limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi) and complete lack of probes amplify any injected JVM load - the container reached its CPU ceiling and its memory limit, was OOMKilled, and because no readiness probe exists the pod stayed Ready and in the Service endpoints, so frontend kept sending GetAds traffic to an unresponsive endpoint and got sub-2ms rejections.

Alternative candidate not confirmed: the flagd fault flags adHighCpu ("Triggers high cpu load in the ad service") and adManualGc ("Triggers full manual garbage collections in the ad service") in the otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap declare exactly the CPU/GC signature seen on the ad JVM. The ConfigMap read at query time shows both defaultVariant "off", flagd container logs returned no lines for 09:10-09:28, and change history is not an available data source, so I could not verify whether either flag was enabled during the incident.

Rejected as the cause: a resource problem in frontend or frontend-proxy. The frontend's CPU throttling ratio (~0.29-0.33) and memory (~126-129 MB of 200Mi) were flat across 09:00-09:28, and frontend-proxy's span volume stayed ~7,000 non-error spans per 5 minutes; only the ad-dependent operations errored.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the fraud-detection OOMKilled restart at 08:54:41Z. It occurred ~23 minutes before the frontend-proxy error signal deviated, and fraud-detection's own error spans stayed at ~1.1 per 5 minutes with its UNSET span volume unchanged (~360-450 per 5 minutes).

Not all frontend-proxy errors are new: 1-4.4 error spans per 5 minutes existed before 09:17 and the access logs contain sparse 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started entries from 08:52 to 09:10; those baseline errors are background and are far smaller than the 138-661 per 5 minutes that appear from 09:19.

Read the actual injected fault from the chaos objects (kubectl get schedule,jvmchaos -n chaos-mesh otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos -o yaml and its child jobs) and from chaos-controller-manager/chaos-daemon logs, to confirm the JVM action (CPU stress, memory stress, GC, latency or exception) and whether it is still running.

Add a gRPC readiness probe (and liveness/startup probes) to the ad Deployment so an unresponsive JVM is removed from the ad Service endpoints, and raise the ad container's CPU limit above 50m and its memory limit above 450Mi, since the ad JVM saturates 50m CPU and exceeded 450Mi during this incident.

Verify the flagd flag state during 09:16-09:28 (flagd UI/ConfigMap revision history or flagd logs) for adHighCpu and adManualGc, since both declare the observed CPU/GC failure mode but currently read as off.

gaps: The JVMChaos/Schedule specs could not be read: those kinds are not in the readable Kubernetes kinds, so the injected action, target method and duration of otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos are unknown.

chaos-controller-manager (chaos-controller-manager-79db7b46c5-24rkp) and chaos-daemon (chaos-daemon-w7ws4, the daemon on node i-06e4f0f4f681d7e45) log reads for 09:15-09:28 returned zero lines, so there is no controller-side confirmation of the injected fault.

A fetch of the ad container's logs for 09:17:11-09:28:53 (after the restart) returned zero lines, so post-restart application behaviour of the new JVM cannot be seen; the previous container's logs are no longer available on the node.

flagd container logs returned zero lines for 09:10-09:28, so the flag values in effect during the incident are unverified; the change-history integration is not available in this Run, so pre-window ConfigMap/Deployment edits cannot be checked.
list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing, so the exact alert expression, threshold and 'for' duration behind the RequestErrorRate alert could not be confirmed.

Jaeger searches for frontend, frontend-proxy and ad in the incident window returned no traces (empty results), so span-level status messages and error details are unknown; traces_list_services did list those services.
Events after 09:25:41Z were not present in the returned set, so whether the JVM chaos schedule was still applying experiments at 09:28 is unknown.
next_steps: Inspect the Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-chaos and its spawned JVMChaos objects in namespace chaos-mesh to identify the exact injected JVM action and whether it is still active.
Review chaos-controller-manager and chaos-daemon logs on node i-06e4f0f4f681d7e45 for the apply/recover operations on pod ad-554b849958-fcl25 container ad.
Check whether the restarted ad container is listening on 8080 and whether it ever produces startup/request logs, to confirm the service is still down after 09:17:10Z.
Confirm the flagd flag values for adHighCpu and adManualGc during the incident from flagd's own state/history rather than the current ConfigMap.
Consider a change review of the ad Deployment's resource limits (50m CPU / 450Mi) and its missing probes, since both materially shaped this failure.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
